cluster_id.description:
ID of the cluster to create. Must start with a lowercase letter,
use only lowercase letters and numbers, and be at most 10 characters long.
cluster_id.rationale: This is the identifier used to name and reference the cluster. The provider enforces its format, while the chosen identifier does not alter access controls, network exposure, or other security behaviour.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Deleting a cluster can remove compute, storage, networking, and orchestration resources associated with the environment. A generic policy can require deletion_policy to be set to PREVENT to reduce the risk of accidental or unauthorized destruction.

description.rationale: This field only stores descriptive text for the cluster and does not change access control, network exposure, workload execution, or security enforcement.

labels.description:
[Labels](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/labeling-resources) applied
to the cluster. Labels can be used to organize clusters and to filter them
in queries.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Labels are metadata used to organize and filter resources. They do not directly control access, connectivity, workload execution, or other security behaviour.

location.description: Resource ID segment making up resource 'name'. It identifies the resource within its parent collection as described in https://google.aip.dev/122.
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: This selects the Google Cloud project that owns the resource. The appropriate project is environment-specific, so a generic policy cannot safely require one particular project identifier.

compute_resources.description:
Compute resources available to the cluster. Keys specify the ID of the
compute resource by which it can be referenced elsewhere, and must conform
to [RFC-1034](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1034) (lower-case,
alphanumeric, and at most 63 characters).

compute_resources.id.rationale: This is an internal identifier used to reference a compute resource elsewhere in the cluster configuration. It does not itself change the security posture of the compute resource.

compute_resources.config.description: Describes how a compute resource should be created at runtime.

compute_resources.config.new_flex_start_.description:
When set in a ComputeResourceConfig, indicates that VM instances should
be created using [Flex
Start](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/provisioning-models).

Name of the Compute Engine [machine
type](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/machine-resource) to use, e.g.
'n2-standard-2'.
compute_resources.config.new_flex_start_.rationale: This selects the VM machine type used for Flex Start instances. It primarily affects compute capacity, performance, and cost rather than a generic security control.

compute_resources.config.new_flex_start_.description:
Specifies the time limit for created instances. Instances will be
terminated at the end of this duration.
compute_resources.config.new_flex_start_.rationale: This sets how long Flex Start instances may run before termination. It controls workload lifetime and scheduling rather than access control or security enforcement.

compute_resources.config.new_flex_start_.description:
Name of the zone in which VM instances should run, e.g., 'us-central1-a'.
Must be in the same region as the cluster, and must match the zone of any
other resources specified in the cluster.
compute_resources.config.new_flex_start_.rationale: This selects the zone where the instances run and must be consistent with the cluster region and other resources. The appropriate zone is an operational placement choice rather than a generic security policy target.

compute_resources.config.new_on_demand_i.description:
When set in a ComputeResourceConfig, indicates that on-demand (i.e.,
using the standard provisioning model) VM instances should be created.

Name of the Compute Engine [machine
type](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/machine-resource) to use, e.g.
'n2-standard-2'.
compute_resources.config.new_on_demand_i.rationale: This selects the VM machine type for on-demand instances. It affects compute capacity, performance, and cost rather than a generic security control.

compute_resources.config.new_on_demand_i.description:
Name of the zone in which VM instances should run, e.g., 'us-central1-a'.
Must be in the same region as the cluster, and must match the zone of any
other resources specified in the cluster.
compute_resources.config.new_on_demand_i.rationale: This selects the zone where on-demand instances run and must match the cluster's regional placement requirements. The exact zone is an operational deployment choice rather than a generic security control.

compute_resources.config.new_reserved_in.description:
When set in a ComputeResourceConfig, indicates that VM instances should
be created from a
[reservation](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/reservations-overview).

Name of the reservation from which VM instances should be created, in the
format 'projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/reservations/{reservation}'.
compute_resources.config.new_reserved_in.rationale: This identifies the reservation from which VM instances should be created. The correct reservation is environment-specific and relates to capacity allocation rather than generic security enforcement.

compute_resources.config.new_spot_instan.description:
When set in a ComputeResourceConfig, indicates that [spot
VM](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/spot) instances should be
created.

Name of the Compute Engine [machine
type](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/machine-resource) to use, e.g.
'n2-standard-2'.
compute_resources.config.new_spot_instan.rationale: This selects the VM machine type used for Spot instances. It affects capacity, performance, and cost rather than access control or security enforcement.

compute_resources.config.new_spot_instan.description:
Specifies the termination action of the instance
Possible values:
STOP
DELETE
compute_resources.config.new_spot_instan.rationale: This controls whether a Spot VM is stopped or deleted when it is terminated. It is a lifecycle and workload-availability choice rather than a generic security control.

compute_resources.config.new_spot_instan.description:
Name of the zone in which VM instances should run, e.g., 'us-central1-a'.
Must be in the same region as the cluster, and must match the zone of any
other resources specified in the cluster.
compute_resources.config.new_spot_instan.rationale: This selects the zone where Spot instances run and must match the cluster's regional placement requirements. The exact zone is an operational deployment choice rather than a generic security control.

network_resources.description:
Network resources available to the cluster. Must contain at most one value.
Keys specify the ID of the network resource by which it can be referenced
elsewhere, and must conform to
[RFC-1034](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1034) (lower-case,
alphanumeric, and at most 63 characters).

network_resources.id.rationale: This is an internal identifier used to reference the network resource elsewhere in the cluster configuration. It does not itself determine network reachability or enforce a security boundary.

network_resources.config.description:
Describes how a network resource should be initialized. Each network resource
can either be imported from an existing Google Cloud resource or initialized
when the cluster is created.

network_resources.config.existing_networ.description:
When set in a NetworkResourceConfig, indicates that an existing network
should be imported.

Name of the network to import, in the format
'projects/{project}/global/networks/{network}'.
network_resources.config.existing_networ.rationale: This selects an existing VPC network to attach to the cluster. The correct network is specific to the team's architecture and environment, so a generic policy cannot safely require one particular network identifier.

network_resources.config.existing_networ.description:
Particular subnetwork to use, in the format
'projects/{project}/regions/{region}/subnetworks/{subnetwork}'.
network_resources.config.existing_networ.rationale: This selects the existing subnetwork used by the cluster. The appropriate subnetwork is an environment-specific network design and routing choice rather than a generic platform security target.

network_resources.config.new_network.description:
When set in a NetworkResourceConfig, indicates that a new network should
be created.

network_resources.config.new_network.des.description: Description of the network. Maximum of 2048 characters.
network_resources.config.new_network.des.rationale: This field only stores descriptive text for the network and does not change routing, exposure, firewall behaviour, or access control.

network_resources.config.new_network.net.description:
Name of the network to create, in the format
'projects/{project}/global/networks/{network}'.
network_resources.config.new_network.net.rationale: This identifies the VPC network to create for the cluster. The network name is an environment-specific naming and architecture choice and does not by itself enforce a security control.

orchestrator.description:
The component responsible for scheduling and running workloads on the
cluster as well as providing the user interface for interacting with the
cluster at runtime.

orchestrator.slurm.description:
When set in Orchestrator, indicates that the cluster should use
[Slurm](https://slurm.schedmd.com/) as the orchestrator.

orchestrator.slurm.default_partition.description:
Default partition to use for submitted jobs that do not explicitly specify
a partition. Required if and only if there is more than one partition, in
which case it must match the id of one of the partitions.
orchestrator.slurm.default_partition.rationale: This selects which Slurm partition receives jobs that do not explicitly specify one. The correct partition depends on the cluster's workload and scheduling design rather than a universal security requirement.

orchestrator.slurm.epilog_bash_scripts.description:
Slurm [epilog scripts](https://slurm.schedmd.com/prolog_epilog.html), which
will be executed by compute nodes whenever a node finishes running a job.
Values must not be empty.
orchestrator.slurm.epilog_bash_scripts.rationale: Epilog scripts execute commands on compute nodes after jobs finish. Because arbitrary script content can modify the host, access data, or run privileged actions, these scripts directly affect the security posture and should be restricted to approved content.

orchestrator.slurm.prolog_bash_scripts.description:
Slurm [prolog scripts](https://slurm.schedmd.com/prolog_epilog.html), which
will be executed by compute nodes before a node begins running a new job.
Values must not be empty.
orchestrator.slurm.prolog_bash_scripts.rationale: Prolog scripts execute commands on compute nodes before jobs run. Because arbitrary script content can modify the host, access data, or alter workload execution, these scripts directly affect the security posture and should be restricted to approved content.

orchestrator.slurm.login_nodes.description:
Configuration for Slurm [login
nodes](https://slurm.schedmd.com/quickstart_admin.html#login) in the cluster.
Login nodes are Compute Engine VM instances that allow users to access the
cluster over SSH.

orchestrator.slurm.login_nodes.count.description: Number of login node instances to create.
orchestrator.slurm.login_nodes.count.rationale: This controls the number of login node instances. It primarily affects capacity and availability and does not directly determine how users authenticate or whether the nodes are publicly exposed.

orchestrator.slurm.login_nodes.enable_os.description:
Whether [OS Login](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/oslogin) should be
enabled on login node instances.
orchestrator.slurm.login_nodes.enable_os.rationale: OS Login centralizes SSH access using Google Cloud identities and IAM rather than relying only on instance metadata SSH keys. A generic policy can require OS Login on cluster login nodes to strengthen access control and account management.

orchestrator.slurm.login_nodes.enable_pu.description:
Whether login node instances should be assigned [external IP
addresses](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/ip-addresses#externaladdresses).
orchestrator.slurm.login_nodes.enable_pu.rationale: Assigning external IP addresses makes login nodes directly reachable from external networks. A generic security policy can require public IPs to be disabled to reduce unnecessary internet exposure.

orchestrator.slurm.login_nodes.labels.description:
[Labels](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/labeling-resources) that
should be applied to each login node instance.
orchestrator.slurm.login_nodes.labels.rationale: These labels are metadata applied to login node instances for organization and filtering. They do not directly control authentication, network exposure, or workload execution.

orchestrator.slurm.login_nodes.machine_t.description:
Name of the Compute Engine [machine
type](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/machine-resource) to use for
login nodes, e.g. 'n2-standard-2'.
orchestrator.slurm.login_nodes.machine_t.rationale: This selects the VM machine type for login nodes. It affects compute capacity, performance, and cost rather than a generic security control.

orchestrator.slurm.login_nodes.startup_s.description:
[Startup
script](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/startup-scripts/linux)
to be run on each login node instance. Max 256KB.
The script must complete within the system-defined default timeout of 5
minutes. For tasks that require more time, consider running them in the
background using methods such as '&' or 'nohup'.
orchestrator.slurm.login_nodes.startup_s.rationale: The startup script executes commands automatically on each login node when it starts. Arbitrary script content can modify system configuration, credentials, software, and access controls, so it directly affects the node's security posture.

orchestrator.slurm.login_nodes.zone.description:
Name of the zone in which login nodes should run, e.g., 'us-central1-a'.
Must be in the same region as the cluster, and must match the zone of any
other resources specified in the cluster.
orchestrator.slurm.login_nodes.zone.rationale: This selects the zone where login nodes run and must be consistent with other cluster resources. The exact zone is an operational placement choice rather than a generic security control.

orchestrator.slurm.login_nodes.boot_disk.description:
A [Persistent disk](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks) used as the
boot disk for a Compute Engine VM instance.
Size of the disk in gigabytes. Must be at least 10GB.
orchestrator.slurm.login_nodes.boot_disk.rationale: This controls login-node boot disk capacity. It affects storage sizing and cost rather than access control, data exposure, or security enforcement.
This selects the persistent disk type used by login nodes. The appropriate disk type depends on performance and cost requirements and is not a generic security setting.

orchestrator.slurm.login_nodes.storage_c.description:
How storage resources should be mounted on each login
node.

ID of the storage resource to mount, which must match a key in the
cluster's [storage_resources](Cluster.storage_resources).
orchestrator.slurm.login_nodes.storage_c.rationale: This identifies which configured storage resource is mounted on a login node. The correct storage resource is environment-specific and the identifier itself does not define its permissions or security controls.

orchestrator.slurm.login_nodes.storage_c.description:
A directory inside the VM instance's file system where the storage resource
should be mounted (e.g., '/mnt/share').
orchestrator.slurm.login_nodes.storage_c.rationale: This specifies the local filesystem path where a storage resource is mounted. The mount path is an operational filesystem layout choice and does not by itself change the storage resource's access controls.

orchestrator.slurm.node_sets.description:
Configuration of Slurm nodesets, which define groups of compute resources
that can be used by Slurm. At least one compute node is required.

orchestrator.slurm.node_sets.compute_id.description:
ID of the compute resource on which this nodeset will run. Must match a key
in the cluster's [compute_resources](Cluster.compute_resources).
orchestrator.slurm.node_sets.compute_id.rationale: This references the compute resource used by the nodeset. The appropriate compute resource is determined by cluster design and the identifier itself does not enforce a security control.

orchestrator.slurm.node_sets.id.description:
Identifier for the nodeset, which allows it to be referenced by partitions.
Must conform to
[RFC-1034](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1034) (lower-case,
alphanumeric, and at most 63 characters).
orchestrator.slurm.node_sets.id.rationale: This is an identifier used to reference a Slurm nodeset from partitions. It does not directly alter access control, workload privileges, or network exposure.

orchestrator.slurm.node_sets.max_dynamic.description:
Controls how many additional nodes a cluster can bring online to handle
workloads. Set this value to enable dynamic node creation and limit the
number of additional nodes the cluster can bring online. Leave empty if you
do not want the cluster to create nodes dynamically, and instead rely only
on static nodes.
orchestrator.slurm.node_sets.max_dynamic.rationale: This limits the number of additional nodes that Slurm can create dynamically. It is a capacity and scaling control rather than a generic security setting.

orchestrator.slurm.node_sets.static_node.description:
Number of nodes to be statically created for this nodeset. The cluster will
attempt to ensure that at least this many nodes exist at all times.
orchestrator.slurm.node_sets.static_node.rationale: This sets the number of nodes that should exist statically in the nodeset. It primarily affects capacity and availability rather than a generic security control.

orchestrator.slurm.node_sets.compute_ins.description:
When set in a SlurmNodeSet, indicates that the nodeset should be backed
by Compute Engine VM instances.

[Labels](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/labeling-resources) that
should be applied to each VM instance in the nodeset.
orchestrator.slurm.node_sets.compute_ins.rationale: These labels are metadata applied to compute instances for organization and filtering. They do not directly alter access controls, network exposure, or workload privileges.

orchestrator.slurm.node_sets.compute_ins.description:
[Startup
script](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/startup-scripts/linux)
to be run on each VM instance in the nodeset. Max 256KB.
orchestrator.slurm.node_sets.compute_ins.rationale: The startup script executes commands automatically on each compute instance in the nodeset. Arbitrary script content can modify system configuration, software, credentials, or workload behaviour, so it directly affects the security posture.

orchestrator.slurm.node_sets.compute_ins.description:
A [Persistent disk](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks) used as the
boot disk for a Compute Engine VM instance.
Size of the disk in gigabytes. Must be at least 10GB.
orchestrator.slurm.node_sets.compute_ins.rationale: This controls the boot disk capacity of compute instances. It is a storage-sizing and cost choice rather than a generic security control.
This selects the persistent disk type used by compute instances. The appropriate type depends on performance and cost requirements rather than a generic security requirement.

orchestrator.slurm.node_sets.storage_con.description:
How storage resources should be mounted on each compute
node.

ID of the storage resource to mount, which must match a key in the
cluster's [storage_resources](Cluster.storage_resources).
orchestrator.slurm.node_sets.storage_con.rationale: This identifies which configured storage resource is mounted on compute nodes. The correct storage resource is environment-specific and the identifier itself does not define its security controls.

orchestrator.slurm.node_sets.storage_con.description:
A directory inside the VM instance's file system where the storage resource
should be mounted (e.g., '/mnt/share').
orchestrator.slurm.node_sets.storage_con.rationale: This specifies the local filesystem path where a storage resource is mounted on compute nodes. It is an operational filesystem layout choice rather than a generic security control.

orchestrator.slurm.partitions.description:
Configuration of Slurm partitions, which group one or more nodesets. Acts
as a queue against which jobs can be submitted. At least one partition is
required.

orchestrator.slurm.partitions.id.description:
ID of the partition, which is how users will identify it. Must conform to
[RFC-1034](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1034) (lower-case,
alphanumeric, and at most 63 characters).
orchestrator.slurm.partitions.id.rationale: This is the identifier users use to reference a Slurm partition. Naming a partition does not directly alter authentication, authorization, or workload security.

orchestrator.slurm.partitions.node_set_i.description:
IDs of the nodesets that make up this partition. Values must match
SlurmNodeSet.id.
orchestrator.slurm.partitions.node_set_i.rationale: This determines which nodesets belong to a Slurm partition. The appropriate grouping depends on workload scheduling and cluster architecture rather than a universal security requirement.

storage_resources.description:
Storage resources available to the cluster. Keys specify the ID of the
storage resource by which it can be referenced elsewhere, and must conform
to [RFC-1034](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1034) (lower-case,
alphanumeric, and at most 63 characters).

storage_resources.id.rationale: This is an internal identifier used to reference a storage resource elsewhere in the cluster configuration. It does not itself change storage permissions, exposure, or data protection.

storage_resources.config.description:
Describes how a storage resource should be initialized. Each storage resource
can either be imported from an existing Google Cloud resource or initialized
when the cluster is created.

storage_resources.config.existing_bucket.description:
When set in a StorageResourceConfig, indicates that an existing
[Google Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage) bucket should be
imported.
Name of the Cloud Storage bucket to import.
storage_resources.config.existing_bucket.rationale: This selects an existing Cloud Storage bucket to use. The correct bucket is environment-specific, while access control and data-protection settings are managed on the bucket itself rather than through this reference.

storage_resources.config.existing_filest.description:
When set in a StorageResourceConfig, indicates that an existing
[Filestore](https://cloud.google.com/filestore) instance should be imported.

Name of the Filestore instance to import, in the format
'projects/{project}/locations/{location}/instances/{instance}'
storage_resources.config.existing_filest.rationale: This selects an existing Filestore instance to use. The correct instance is environment-specific, while its access and network controls are managed on the Filestore resource itself.

storage_resources.config.existing_lustre.description:
When set in a StorageResourceConfig, indicates that an existing
[Managed Lustre](https://cloud.google.com/products/managed-lustre) instance
should be imported.

Name of the Managed Lustre instance to import, in the format
'projects/{project}/locations/{location}/instances/{instance}'
storage_resources.config.existing_lustre.rationale: This selects an existing Managed Lustre instance to use. The correct instance is environment-specific, while its security controls are managed on the Lustre resource itself.

storage_resources.config.new_bucket.description:
When set in a StorageResourceConfig, indicates that a new
[Google Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage) bucket should be
created.

storage_resources.config.new_bucket.buck.description: Name of the Cloud Storage bucket to create.
storage_resources.config.new_bucket.buck.rationale: This specifies the name of a Cloud Storage bucket to create. The bucket name is an identifier and does not by itself define access control, encryption, or data exposure.

storage_resources.config.new_bucket.stor.description:
If set, uses the provided storage class as the bucket's default storage
class.
Possible values:
STANDARD
NEARLINE
COLDLINE
ARCHIVE
storage_resources.config.new_bucket.stor.rationale: This selects the bucket's storage class and primarily affects data retrieval characteristics and cost. It does not directly control access or data security.

storage_resources.config.new_bucket.auto.description: Message describing Google Cloud Storage autoclass configuration

storage_resources.config.new_bucket.auto.rationale: This enables automatic transitions between Cloud Storage classes based on access patterns. It is a storage lifecycle and cost-management feature rather than a generic security control.

storage_resources.config.new_bucket.auto.description:
Terminal storage class of the autoclass bucket
Possible values:
NEARLINE
ARCHIVE
storage_resources.config.new_bucket.auto.rationale: This selects the terminal storage class used by Autoclass. It affects storage lifecycle and cost characteristics rather than access control or security enforcement.

storage_resources.config.new_bucket.hier.description: Message describing Google Cloud Storage hierarchical namespace configuration
Enables hierarchical namespace setup for the bucket.
storage_resources.config.new_bucket.hier.rationale: This enables hierarchical namespace semantics for the bucket. It changes namespace and filesystem-style behaviour, but the setting alone does not establish a universal access-control or exposure requirement for this cluster resource.

storage_resources.config.new_filestore.description:
When set in a StorageResourceConfig, indicates that a new
[Filestore](https://cloud.google.com/filestore) instance should be created.

storage_resources.config.new_filestore.d.description: Description of the instance. Maximum of 2048 characters.
storage_resources.config.new_filestore.d.rationale: This field only stores descriptive text for the Filestore instance and does not change access control, network exposure, or data protection.

storage_resources.config.new_filestore.f.description:
Name of the Filestore instance to create, in the format
'projects/{project}/locations/{location}/instances/{instance}'
storage_resources.config.new_filestore.f.rationale: This specifies the resource name of the Filestore instance to create. The identifier is environment-specific and does not itself determine the instance's security controls.

storage_resources.config.new_filestore.p.description:
Access protocol to use for all file shares in the instance. Defaults to NFS
V3 if not set.
Possible values:
NFSV3
NFSV41 Possible values: ["PROTOCOL_UNSPECIFIED", "NFSV3", "NFSV41"]
storage_resources.config.new_filestore.p.rationale: This selects the NFS protocol version used by the Filestore instance. The appropriate protocol depends on client compatibility and workload requirements, and this Cluster Director field does not expose a universal security policy target by itself.

storage_resources.config.new_filestore.t.description:
Service tier to use for the instance.
Possible values:
ZONAL
REGIONAL Possible values: ["TIER_UNSPECIFIED", "ZONAL", "REGIONAL"]
storage_resources.config.new_filestore.t.rationale: This selects the Filestore service tier and primarily affects availability, placement, and performance characteristics rather than a generic security control.

storage_resources.config.new_filestore.f.description:
File system shares on the instance. Exactly one file share must be
specified.

Size of the filestore in GB. Must be between 1024 and 102400, and must meet
scalability requirements described at
https://cloud.google.com/filestore/docs/service-tiers.
storage_resources.config.new_filestore.f.rationale: This controls the storage capacity of the Filestore share. It is a sizing and cost setting rather than a generic security control.
This names the Filestore share location. The name is an operational identifier and does not itself control who can access the share.

storage_resources.config.new_lustre.description:
When set in a StorageResourceConfig, indicates that a new
[Managed Lustre](https://cloud.google.com/products/managed-lustre) instance
should be created.

storage_resources.config.new_lustre.capa.description:
Storage capacity of the instance in gibibytes (GiB). Allowed values are
between 18000 and 7632000.
storage_resources.config.new_lustre.capa.rationale: This controls the capacity of the Managed Lustre instance. It is a sizing and cost setting rather than a generic security control.

storage_resources.config.new_lustre.desc.description: Description of the Managed Lustre instance. Maximum of 2048 characters.
storage_resources.config.new_lustre.desc.rationale: This field only stores descriptive text for the Managed Lustre instance and does not change access control, network exposure, or data protection.

storage_resources.config.new_lustre.file.description:
Filesystem name for this instance. This name is used by client-side tools,
including when mounting the instance. Must be 8 characters or less and can
only contain letters and numbers.
storage_resources.config.new_lustre.file.rationale: This sets the filesystem name used by clients and mounting tools. It is an operational identifier and does not itself define authentication, authorization, or network exposure.

storage_resources.config.new_lustre.lust.description:
Name of the Managed Lustre instance to create, in the format
'projects/{project}/locations/{location}/instances/{instance}'
storage_resources.config.new_lustre.lust.rationale: This specifies the resource name of the Managed Lustre instance to create. The identifier is environment-specific and does not itself determine access controls or data protection.

storage_resources.config.new_lustre.per_.description:
Throughput of the instance in MB/s/TiB. Valid values are 125, 250,
500, 1000. See [Performance tiers and maximum storage
capacities](https://cloud.google.com/managed-lustre/docs/create-instance#performance-tiers)
for more information.
storage_resources.config.new_lustre.per_.rationale: This sets the storage throughput tier for the Managed Lustre instance. It controls performance characteristics rather than access control, exposure, or other security enforcement.
